boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named DePauw spaces for quiet work, group projects, meetings, creative production and reflection, with campus-specific uses documented by university sources.

cards.title: Match the Room to the Assignment
cards.subtitle: Private rooms, collaboration areas and quiet corners at Roy O.
cards.notes: Reserve a study room for group work, or scout the reading room and solo workstations when the assignment calls for fewer distractions.
cards.short_summary: A renovated library offering distinct settings for solo study, collaborative work and multimedia projects.
cards.evidence_claim: DePauw says Roy O. West Library has solo workstations, private study rooms, more than 40 student-collaboration areas, a meditation room and a reading room.
cards.source_title: Roy O. West Library | Virtual Tour
cards.access_notes: At 11 E. Larabee St.; consult the library’s current hours and room-reservation system before visiting.

cards.title: Build a Flexible Union-Building Routine
cards.subtitle: Games, quiet study and organization meetings under one roof
cards.notes: Use the Union’s recreation areas for a break, then shift to a quiet spot or the campus-life meeting area for focused work.
cards.short_summary: The student union combines informal recreation, quiet study and reservable group activity space.
cards.evidence_claim: DePauw’s housing FAQ says the Union Building offers arcades, television or video games, quiet study space and a campus-life meeting area for student groups.
cards.access_notes: After-hours building access may require a DePauw ID card; verify current access before planning a late session.

cards.title: Keep Pulliam in the Exam-Week Rotation
cards.subtitle: A media building that DePauw also designates for extended study
cards.notes: Check Pulliam when regular rooms fill during finals, and bring your DePauw ID because card access applies during some extended hours.
cards.short_summary: An academic media center that becomes an officially designated extended-hours study location during finals.
cards.evidence_claim: DePauw’s Spring 2026 finals page lists the Pulliam Center as a 24-hour study space and notes that ID-card access is required during some hours.
cards.source_title: Final Exams Study Hours and Spaces
cards.access_notes: The cited 24-hour designation applies to Spring 2026 finals; some hours require a DePauw ID card.

cards.entity_name: Percy Lavon Julian Science and Mathematics Center
cards.title: Spread Out in Julian’s Atrium
cards.subtitle: A three-story science-center commons with study space
cards.notes: Try the east-entry atrium when you need an academic setting with room to spread out and network access for collaborative problem-solving.
cards.short_summary: A science-building atrium designed with abundant connected study space beyond its classrooms and laboratories.
cards.evidence_claim: DePauw’s university catalog page says Julian’s east entrance opens into a three-story atrium with abundant study space and wired and wireless network access.
cards.access_notes: Classroom-building access can depend on the academic calendar and student card-swipe rules.

cards.entity_name: Justin and Darrianne Christian Center for Diversity and Inclusion
cards.title: Choose a CDI Room by Group Size
cards.subtitle: Named lounges, meeting rooms, study space and a kitchen
cards.notes: Review the room list before gathering: choose Bennett Library for a small study group or reserve a media lounge when technology matters.
cards.short_summary: A student center with clearly defined spaces for studying, meetings, cooking and campus programming.
cards.evidence_claim: DePauw lists CDI spaces including Bennett Library for reading and study, two media lounges, a student study room, meeting rooms and a dining room with kitchen.
cards.access_notes: Many spaces use a reservation process; review CDI policy and submit the official request before hosting a group.

cards.title: Use the Lounge to Connect or Reset
cards.subtitle: A reservable living-room setting at 306 East Hanna Street
cards.notes: Stop in for quiet study or connection, and reserve the lounge when a club, class or recurring group needs a comfortable meeting place.
cards.short_summary: A historic-house campus center with a spacious lounge, kitchen and programming for people of all genders.
cards.evidence_claim: DePauw says the Women’s Center welcomes people of all genders, provides a spacious living room and full kitchen, and makes its lounge available to groups, clubs and classes.
cards.access_notes: At 306 E. Hanna St.; academic-year hours are Monday-Friday, 10 a.m.-10 p.m., with separate summer office hours posted.

cards.title: Find a Room for Reflection or Prayer
cards.subtitle: The Center for Spiritual Life at 411 East Seminary Street
cards.notes: Choose among the interfaith, Muslim, Hindu, Buddhist, Jewish and Christian prayer rooms according to your own reflective practice.
cards.short_summary: A swipe-access spiritual-life house supporting multiple faith traditions as well as people without a religious affiliation.
cards.evidence_claim: DePauw identifies Bartlett House as the Center for Spiritual Life and lists meditation or interfaith space plus Muslim, Hindu, Buddhist, Jewish and Christian prayer rooms.
cards.access_notes: DePauw lists swipe access seven days a week from 6 a.m. to midnight; access is intended for the university community.

cards.entity_name: James and Sue Bartlett Reflection Center
cards.title: Pair Quiet Time With a Quarry View
cards.subtitle: A reflection center inside the DePauw Nature Park
cards.notes: Use the labyrinth and yoga room or the separate meditation room, then allow enough daylight and travel time for the Nature Park setting.
cards.short_summary: A purpose-built reflection space whose rooms overlook the Nature Park’s quarry pond.
cards.evidence_claim: DePauw says the Bartlett Reflection Center contains a labyrinth, yoga and viewing room overlooking the quarry pond plus a meditation room with religious texts and prayer tools.
cards.access_notes: DePauw lists swipe access Monday-Friday, 9 a.m.-5 p.m., and access by request outside that arrangement.

cards.title: Prototype With Tools Beyond a Laptop
cards.subtitle: Collaborative technology facilities inside Roy O. West Library
cards.notes: Bring a digital project to Tenzer when advanced computers or hands-on technology would improve the work; check training requirements first.
cards.short_summary: A cross-disciplinary technology center for collaborative computing, visualization and hands-on digital projects.
cards.evidence_claim: DePauw describes Tenzer as a high-tech collaborative space available to the entire university community, with advanced technology, workshops and mentoring.
cards.access_notes: Located in Roy O. West Library; individual equipment and maker spaces may require orientation, training or staff guidance.

cards.title: Take Focused Work Into the Nature Park
cards.subtitle: A finals study option beyond the central campus buildings
cards.notes: Plan the trip when a change of setting would help concentration, and confirm building hours plus a safe route before leaving campus.
cards.short_summary: A Nature Park institute that DePauw includes among its official exam-period study locations.
cards.evidence_claim: DePauw’s Spring 2026 finals guide lists the Prindle Institute for Ethics among its suggested study spaces, with weekday hours of 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.
cards.source_title: Final Exams Study Hours and Spaces
cards.access_notes: The cited 8 a.m.-5 p.m. schedule applies Monday-Thursday during Spring 2026 finals; verify current hours and transportation.
